section_summary: This section covers the reorganization of Japan’s national tax administration and a 1949 survey of national and local taxation, including tax rates, revenues, enforcement and government monopolies. Later documents examine how Japanese taxes and customs duties might affect foreign businesses and investment.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 319 on reorganization of Japanese national tax administration
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports the expected establishment of a new Tax Administration Bureau and encloses SCAPIN 2001.
subfiles.summary: Mr. Moss expected the new bureau to be established by June 1.

subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2001: Reorganization of National Tax Administration
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The directive orders a professional national tax administration with clearer authority over regional and local offices.
subfiles.summary: SCAP directs creation of an external Tax Administration Bureau, transfer of tax functions, retention of legislative research within the Finance Ministry, and better qualified enforcement personnel.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 330: Transmittal of Memorandum entitled “General Survey of Japanese Taxation”
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards a tax survey prepared for the Shoup Mission and discusses its objectives and findings.
subfiles.summary: Huston describes the mission’s goals of stability, equity, local autonomy and stronger enforcement. He highlights rising estimated tax burdens, uncertainty in national income estimates, and the importance of Japanese tax collections to economic rehabilitation.

subfiles.title: General Survey of Japanese Taxation
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.to: Department of the Army tax survey mission
subfiles.about: The report surveys the development, operation and revenues of Japan’s national and local tax systems.
subfiles.summary: The survey traces tax changes from the prewar period through 1949, covering income, corporate, commodity, transaction and local taxes. It compares collections with national income and describes weak assessment and enforcement, proposed administrative reform, military government surveillance, and taxpayer education. It also reviews Monopoly Bureau revenues and local governments’ tax sources and borrowing concerns.

subfiles.title: Appendix A: Personal Income Tax Rates
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: The appendix lists personal income tax brackets, deductions and credits.
subfiles.summary: Lists graduated rates and provisions for earned income, dependents, capital gains and dividends.

subfiles.title: Appendix B: Commodity Tax Rates
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: The appendix groups taxable commodities by rate.
subfiles.summary: Lists examples of goods in commodity tax groups ranging from 20 to 100 percent.

subfiles.title: Appendix C: Liquor Tax Rates
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: The appendix compares taxes and prices for alcoholic beverages.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates rates and prices for sake, mirin, shochu, beer and whiskey.

subfiles.title: Appendix D: Tax Burdens of Japan
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: The appendix compares tax revenues with estimated national income.
subfiles.summary: Shows rising national and local tax collections as a share of national income.

subfiles.title: Appendix E: Monthly Revenue of Taxes and Stamps for 1948–1949
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: The appendix tabulates monthly receipts by tax category.
subfiles.summary: Lists monthly income, corporation, liquor, commodity and other tax and stamp revenues.

subfiles.title: Appendix F: SCAPIN 2001, Reorganization of National Tax Administration
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The appendix reproduces the directive on reorganizing national tax administration.
subfiles.summary: Orders a new tax bureau, regional restructuring and qualified enforcement staff.

subfiles.title: Appendix G: Japanese Monopoly Bureau
subfiles.from: William Bass, Chief, Monopoly Miscellaneous Revenues
subfiles.about: The memorandum describes the Monopoly Bureau’s organization, products and revenues.
subfiles.summary: It explains the planned conversion to a public corporation and the government’s control of tobacco, salt and camphor. A table records revenues from those products.

subfiles.title: Appendix H: Revenues of Local Governments
subfiles.from: Internal Revenue Division, Economic and Scientific Section
subfiles.about: The appendix tabulates local government revenues from 1945–46 through 1949–50.
subfiles.summary: Lists taxes, fees, loans, shared taxes and subsidies, with notes on sources and estimates.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese taxation of commercial entrants
subfiles.about: The note summarizes proposals to reduce the tax obstacles facing foreign businesses in Japan.
subfiles.summary: It reviews Henry Shavell’s memorandum, the exemption of non-yen income, heavy income and corporate taxes, and untaxed cigarette and liquor imports. It favors addressing foreign investment through broader tax reform and applying duties to non-occupation imports, while summarizing suggestions from Socony-Vacuum representatives.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 417: Japanese Taxation of Commercial Entrants as Related to Question of Attraction of Foreign Capital Investment to Japan
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch forwards Shavell’s memorandum and reports discussion of taxes affecting foreign investment.
subfiles.summary: It describes SCAP’s request for views on commercial entrants, import taxes and preferential treatment. The June 17 discussion focused on cigarette and liquor imports; these pages end while the despatch continues.
